chunks: No equal has He, and with that I am commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims.
ai.seo_question: Who is the first Muslim according to the Quran?
ai.summary: This verse, often cited in Shia tradition as a declaration of the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) exclusive mission, underscores the purity of monotheism (Tawhid) free from any divine partners. By identifying himself as the 'first of the Muslims,' the Prophet establishes his role as the primordial exemplar of submission, a concept that resonates with the Shia understanding of his leadership (Imamate) and the continuity of divine guidance. This statement serves as a foundational proof for the authority of the Prophet in conveying the core message of Islam.
